Five directions for the film, each written shot by shot with reference frames, each built for one commercial job: turn the parent who approves and pays for the lease into the person pushing for the move, and hand her a link to send. Pick one and we go straight to full boards and production. The first direction is the one we recommend, and the reasoning is on its page.

How We Read The Brief
The job

Fill beds. CSL sells to students; this film recruits the person who actually approves and pays for the lease: the parent. The target is a mother in the GTA, Durham, Ottawa or Waterloo whose daughter commutes from home. She made the sensible choice and she has noticed what it costs. The film's one commercial move is to turn her from the reason her daughter commutes into the person pushing for the move, and then hand her a URL to send. Every direction in this doc is scored against that outcome, not against how pretty it is.

The two rules, and how every direction holds them
1

Nothing on screen that smells like a study

No statistics, no research, no numbers, no burned-in claims. Every parent already believes the commute costs her kid something; the moment we cite a source we become an advertisement. Directions 02 to 05 carry their argument entirely in picture, sound and one closing line; Direction 01 carries two short text cards at CSL’s request, the one agreed exception.

2

The enemy is the commute, never the parent

She made a reasonable choice with what she knew. In every direction the daughter is tired, never neglected; the mother is present, never blamed. Since forwarding is effectively the media plan, every shot is tested against: would she send this to her daughter?

Craft standards that apply to whichever direction wins
Color
The grade is the argument. Commute world runs cold, dark and blue; the four-minutes-away world runs warm, bright and safe. Wardrobe follows: baggier, heavier layers in the commute; casual and light at the apartment.
Voice
The mother's voice on a phone call, not a narrator and not text cards. It keeps the film a story, keeps the parent inside it, and gives the cutdowns a natural spine. If a direction plays stronger silent, we argue for silent. Direction 01’s two text cards are the client-requested exception.
End line
Our recommendation stays close to the brief's instinct: "She doesn't get these hours back" then the URL, small. "Give them the time they deserve" reads as an instruction to the parent, and instructed parents don't forward films.
Naming
The film never names a year of study, a school, or a program. Any campus shown stays generic Ontario.
Our recommendation
Direction 01, The Move: the commute, the decision, and the life four minutes from class, in one continuous story.
It keeps the matched-cut discipline (the alarm, the walk, the classroom each answered across the halves) but adds the one thing the parallel versions never had: the decision itself. The viewer watches the move happen, so the film hands her the next step instead of implying it. Built from CSL’s own generated draft frames.

Direction 01
01
The Move
Recommended

One student, one continuous story: the commuting life until she can't, the decision, and the life four minutes from class. Part one runs cold, part two runs warm, and three mirrored shots stitch the halves together (the alarm and the last sleep, the snow walk and the class walk, the stressed lecture and the study lounge). Two short text cards, placed at CSL's request, carry the argument in words exactly twice.

How it sells
The full CSL purchase journey is on screen: the tour, the keys, the roommates, the amenities in use, and the call every paying parent wants back. The parent watching doesn't just feel the difference; she sees exactly what doing something about it looks like.
Why this one
It's the story CSL's buyer actually lives, decision included. The film shows the move itself, so it hands the viewer the next step instead of implying it.

02
Two Fridays

One student. The same Friday, twice: first the commuting version end to end, then the four-minutes-from-class version, shot for shot. The mother's voice arrives as a phone call late in each half. The audience is never told anything; they watch the same day answered.

How it sells
It sells CSL's actual product: proximity. "Four minutes from class" is the whole warm half, and the amenity floor, the roommates and the dinner at six are CSL inventory on screen the entire time. The parent lands on the site already convinced of the one thing a floor plan can't show her.
Why this one
The matched cuts do the persuading, so the film never has to claim anything.

Direction 03
03
One Friday, Intercut

The same two lives, but braided instead of stacked: cold shot, warm answer, cold shot, warm answer, accelerating as the day goes on. Built for feeds, where the first five seconds decide everything; the contrast lands immediately instead of at the halfway turn, and it opens the door to true split-screen moments, both Fridays on screen at once.

SplitBoth Fridays at once
5:58pmThe library · Cold
9:00pmIntramurals · Warm
BeatStructure
0:00–0:08The wake-up pair, back to back. 5:40am dark alarm, hard cut, 8:15am light. The film teaches its grammar in the first eight seconds.
0:08–0:28Morning braid. Quiet dark kitchen / coffee with roommates. Bus glass / the four-minute walk. Late to the back row / early with the group. Each pair cuts on matched action.
0:28–0:45Evening braid, faster. 5:58 library scramble / dinner at six and the library at seven. Alone on the night bus / a gym where her name gets shouted. The cold shots get shorter each round; the warm ones breathe.
0:45–0:58The kitchens. The one pair held long: silent phone face-up / the same kitchen ringing with a full room behind her voice. The mother's call is the only dialogue in the film.
0:58–1:04End card. "She doesn't get these hours back." URL small.
How it sells
Built for paid reach. The contrast lands in the first ten seconds, which is what converts on paid social where CSL can actually buy placement. Same proximity-and-amenity inventory on screen as Direction 02, delivered at feed speed.
Trade-off
Stronger hook, softer ache. Intercutting wins the scroll but gives up the slow accumulation that makes the two-half version land in the chest. If the media plan leans paid social over forwarding, this is the pick.

Direction 04
04
The Photo Wall

The simplest telling: the comparison collapses into one object. A nearly blank wall above a childhood bed becomes, by the end, a wall she can't fit another photo on. Warmer and lighter than the other two directions; it sells what she gains more than what the commute takes, and it ends on the line a parent most wants to hear.

OpenThe blank wall · Cold
TurnKeys · Warm
CloseThe full wall · Warm
BeatStructure
0:00–0:08Open cold. Her childhood bedroom at dusk, blue and quiet. She looks at a wall holding two lonely polaroids. Outside, a moving truck idles.
0:08–0:18The turn. Move-in day: keys from the property manager, a roommate takes a polaroid of the moment. First photo goes up on a new, empty wall.
0:18–0:45The wall fills. Every scene ends with a photo being pinned: dinner spots with the building in the background, the game room, the gym, an intramural jersey, the study room at midnight, a community night. The wall is the clock.
0:45–0:58Close warm. A karaoke night. The camera pulls back from the party to find the wall, now full. On the phone, over the noise: "Hey Mom, I think I love it here." Her mother's short laugh answers.
0:58–1:04End card. "Get their time back" · canadianstudentliving.ca
How it sells
The amenity showcase. Game room, gym, study room, community night: the most direct on-screen tour of what a CSL lease actually buys, wrapped in the line every paying parent wants to hear back.
Trade-off
Warmest and safest, least ache. Without the commute on screen the film argues by absence, so it persuades the parent already halfway there. As a companion piece behind Direction 02 or 03 it would work hard; alone it carries less of the brief's weight.

Direction 05
05
The Moment Before
Reference-led option

A CSL interpretation of the emotional mechanism in Mattamy Homes’ The Moment Before: a familiar property tour plays in the present while the student quietly imagines the life each space could unlock. The apartment is not presented as the finish line. It is the place where the next version of her begins.

ReferenceThe held breath
ReferenceWaiting for what comes next
ReferenceThe ordinary tour
MechanismPresent and possibility
MechanismThe future breaks through
PayoffA life, not a floor plan
TimeThe shotThe job
0:00–0:08Mom and daughter arrive for a CSL tour after the daughter’s long commute. The leasing agent opens the door: “You’re four minutes from class.”Starts in a recognizable purchase moment and places the parent inside the decision.
0:08–0:18In the bedroom, the daughter looks toward the window. For one breath, the empty room becomes tomorrow morning: sunlight, no alarm in the dark, coffee with a roommate.The room becomes returned time, not square footage.
0:18–0:30The agent shows the study lounge. Sound falls away. We glimpse the daughter at the same table with a group, prepared, laughing, then walking into class early.Turns an amenity into the academic and social life the parent wants for her.
0:30–0:42Gym, kitchen, amenity floor. Each practical tour detail triggers a flash of future life: a workout, dinner with roommates, a call home she has time to make.Builds value through possibility while naturally showcasing CSL inventory.
0:42–0:53Back in the empty bedroom. Mom sees what her daughter is seeing. A small look between them. Mom asks, “Can you see yourself here?” The daughter nods.Makes the parent the person who opens the door, never the obstacle.
0:53–1:00The daughter steps across the threshold. Match cut to the same step on move-in day, roommates pulling her inside.The moment before becomes the first moment of the life ahead.
End card
“Four minutes from class. A whole life ahead.”
Get their time back · canadianstudentliving.ca
How it sells
It makes the tour emotionally productive. Every bedroom and amenity is tied to an outcome the parent can picture: better mornings, stronger study habits, friendships, and time to call home. The lease becomes an investment in who her daughter is becoming.
What we borrow
The reference’s held-breath pacing, the collision between an ordinary tour and imagined possibility, and the belief-in-what-comes-next idea. The characters, script, situations, visual grammar, and final line remain distinctly CSL.
Trade-off
Most aspirational, least direct about the pain. It needs disciplined casting and performance to keep the imagined future specific rather than generic. It is a strong brand film, but Direction 01 remains the harder conversion argument.

Production & Schedule
How it gets made

AI-generated production under tight creative direction: one consistent lead across every shot, the cold/warm grade built into generation rather than fixed in post, and every frame reviewed against the two rules before it reaches a cut. Where a shot won't hold to standard, we say so early and swap in licensed or shot footage rather than ship a frame that breaks the film. Music and cutting rhythm stay identical across both worlds, exactly as the brief asks.

Deliverables, and where each one sells
  • Hero film, 50 to 70 seconds, captions burned in: the piece parents forward, and the anchor for the site and YouTube
  • Cutdowns at :30, :15 and :06, each built for its placement: the paid social and retargeting layer that drives tour bookings. Contents planned with you once the direction is picked
  • Six stills, pulled from the chosen direction's strongest frames: listings, organic social, and on-site leasing pages
What we need from CSL

  • Brand assets: logo, colors, and the final URL for the end card
  • Which properties or amenity spaces should be recognizable, if any
